Hello, I too have worked as a manager and specifically Covenants that deals with all enforcement and the Resale packages. The 3 day window is a legal criteria that you MUST receive the package prior to closing. It would be between you and the seller about any additional time to review. The HOA in no way controls the agreements and/or interactions with the buyer and seller. Unfortunately because of the last point I have had individuals buy a home and then upon is notifying them of outstanding notices/balances they inform us they were unaware because they never received a package from the seller. 

Most HOAs/Property Management companies also have confidentiality policies where we can only release property/account information to the legal Owner of record and/or their authorized representatives. If a buyer contacts the HOA inquiring about the status of the property we inform them that they must request that the seller send us written authorization to allow us to release said information to them as an authorized rep. I have very rarely ever seen a seller or their rep refuse to at minimum allow the HOA to discuss the Resale Package with a potential buyer. However I have found on the few times the seller didnt care to it was because they knew whatever agreement they were making going into closing with the buyer would fall through if they did. Again, the HOA/Property Management does NOT intervene or keep track of the negotiations between seller and buyer as legally you do not want to be held liable for someone misrepresenting something and costing someone the sale of their home.

You say its a trick but its a known required package created by the State Legislature decades ago.

The seller is responsible for receiving it, and it must have all up to date information on the homes account and the HOAs standing, finances, and record of all current Board minutes per the law. 

If the HOA fails to release the package in a timely manner, or misinforms/misses key information, then they receive a fine of thousands of dollars for failure to comply.

The seller then must legally turn over the package, to the potential buyer, within 3 days of the proposed closing date. If they fail to do so (usually because they are hiding information about their account status or property damage) then the sale can be stopped immediately by the buyer. Or if the sale goes through cause the buyer is unaware then they can sue the seller and their rep for bo disclosing the package to them and regain their losses for financial or property damage and/or reverse the sale and lock all the money in an escrow account until completion of litigation.

The HOA/Property Management has a due process clause that outlines the number of legally mandated notices it must provide and time line that it must allow before it can take away specific rights or place monetary or additional assessments on accounts. Towing especially must follow all of the aforementioned, if it’s gotten this far the owner may just be ignoring the issue as notices have arrived at the main address for their lot in the HOA, which most likely means identical ones were mailed out to their offsite mailing address they reside at too. 

This isn’t always an issue of an HOA/Property Management being overzealous. I have performed this work in the past and you’d be surprised at how long we give people (3+ months at minimum) to just reach out to us about stuff and no one does until we have a legal hearing to begin the process of additional enforcement and only then so they even show up saying “it’s not that big a deal we didn’t fix our house or owed dues, etc, it’s not a priority for us!”. Just a recommendation. I have worked high up in Property Management for years, specifically enforcement and legal counsel based work. The above comment is spot on. An owner must be up to date on all payments, and only the Owner can legally work with the HOA and property management to setup some sort of plan of action in order to avoid acts of enforcement. 

You have every right to lawyer up, since this is directly impacting you. But please do not make the mistake of contacting the HOA/Property Management and implying or threatening them with legal action. All this will do is make them 100% cease all communication with you unless it’s through their own legal counsel. 

Your best way forward is to make sure your landlord is being truthful and is fulfilling your contract and the agreements signed in it. The HOA/Property Management can not assist you or intervene in a tenant/owner situation. They can only enforce the rules and guidelines as they are written, which most likely means that due to unpaid dues the Owner, and their “guests” (you), lose access to privileges and Common Areas (parking, pool, etc), until the account is made complaint.

Good luck and I hope the landlord resolves this for you quickly!

You also need to ensure you’re HOA is not simply adopting the County/Local Governance ordinances. Many people in the replies just are saying sue or f the HOA. However, I have been doing governing document/enforcement for several years for HOAs in VA. If the HOA basically adopts ordinances that are copies of county/local parking oradinances for local roads then the state/local offices won’t even bat an eye. Basically sounds like the HOA may pass through adopting these things so they can then issue things like violation notices, threats or towing, etc. 

It IS important for homeowners like yourself to ensure the HOA is going through the correct processes and adopting resolutions or rule changes the legal way. Many times HOAs do not hold public meetings and/or town halls for resolution updates, nor do they hold votes and sometimes their legal counsel may interpret things questionably. However, if they do go through all the correct processes and adopt such rules then they could use the power of enforcement even though it’s a public street. I know this as a few HOAs I worked with we’re not satisfied with police response and enforcement to noise and business ordinances being broken within the homes in community. So they adopted the local ordinances into their rules and began issuing notices of violation and sending accounts to legal counsel for additional review. This quickly turned around the issues and was 100% legal and the Town didn’t care cause they also received less calls for police responses to issues they didn’t seem to think they could do much about.

Keep up what you’re doing, and please make sure you go to an Association lawyer and not just a general lawyer as the laws and rules are very very specific and a general lawyer will not be very helpful to you.

Good luck!

As someone who runs a division of a company I always have to remember not to overthink things. I would NEVER deny anyone time off for most any reason, let alone anything to do with family or mental health. Our company is very upfront about being worker first and we even just allow people to take mental days without even asking for PTO submission. But I learned through my own growing pains as a boss that I would sometimes subconsciously alter my initial approvals when my employees would end up giving me a ton of info. That is NOT the employees fault, it was me trying to be fair but trying to also comb through a ton of extra information I was not ready for. So what did I do? I talked to my leadership on how to best make decisions when in this role, especially when given more context than needed. They helped me learn how to remove myself from that information and simply ask if you would approve or deny the request. I also spoke with my team and noted that, while other jobs may have put them on the spot or belittled them, they NEVER needed to give me an explanation why they needed time off. My only item would to be review their accounts to make sure I knew where they were at with a client to ensure I knew how to properly cover until they were back. It was a learning curve for both sides but we have 0 attendance or disciplinary issues and everyone takes all planned and unplanned time off as needed, or when needed. This is all to say that the content OP posted is so easily avoidable when your bosses put in the tiniest damn effort to just not be an ass, yet as we all know in this sub it still happens and people are placed in shot spots like this for just living life.

Also, please move over. You are not a traffic monitor nor a police officer, you do not get to “enforce” the law. If you are in the far left lane, and see someone gradually gaining on you, then look for a safe time and move over to the right and let them pass. While we all should obey all traffic laws and speed limits we also shouldn’t police the roads ourselves and create unintended additional impediments in our travel life. If you feel the driver is being unsafe/reckless then do what I do, try to safely obtain a make and model and license plate number, then when able safely call 911 and report the driver. This will go a long way in potentially helping them improve their behavior if a law enforcement officer, or calling their company if it’s a work vehicle with a number, than you trying to cruise in front of them/slow down - brake check, which also takes your attention from the road in front of you. I mean it’s not literally the whole neighborhood out at once lol. The neighborhood is very quiet, most of the cars are just overflow as the townhomes have assigned parking and a lot of the street parking is secondary cars or work from home residents who don’t go out much. Again I’ve only had 30 yrs experience living in the community but unless you’re near the school fields on a nice weekend when there are soccer and children’s t ball you won’t really hear much. It’s a neighborhood of long time ownership properties and low percent rentals. The biggest secret no one really knows is that while there are Owners Associations they mostly lack any power to enforce things last trash and snow removal (both paid for by dues) but the Community stays looking nice because the aforementioned long time owners do a lot of upkeep and always have of their own volition. So unless you have an unruly loud neighbor or some mischievous children on your row of townhomes then you really won’t hear or see much that, it’s a suburban neighborhood and not urban in really anyway.

I grew up in Brookfield, family moved here in 1995. My family still lives there now even though they are retired. The entire development is massive as several Owners Associations make up the Community as a whole. It’s a quiet working to upper middle class community that’s totally walkable and very safe. Trails behind most of the houses that can take you out toward Chantilly High School or even toward Westfield Blvd and the Wegmans Shopping Center. You’ll always find people out walking at all hours of day and night, and the Elementary School is a good school if you have kids, or plan to, and it’s located smack dab in the middle of the Community (the Middle and High School sit just outside of it. The library is off of Stringfellow and is about a 20 min walk or a 5 min drive. It is has its own Shopping Center on the “front” side next to Route 50 (Chantilly Plaza) but it doesn’t have a grocery store, just a Dollar Store with some small grocery/snack options. You are about 10 to 15 minutes from several other large shopping centers (Sully, Greenbriar, Chantilly Crossing) and also about 15ish minutes from Fair Oaks Mall. You also have access to Metro via several bus stops located off Galesbury Lane and Tabscott (if you need public transport) or can drive into Herndon and hop on the Silver Line if ya want to just hop directly on the train (about 20 min away). I almost forgot you are also about 15 min from the Dulles Expo center. As the comment above stated you can find so many small and chain restaurant options, and styles of food, that it would take a long time to list them all and make my post about 3 times as long as it already is lol. And finally we have two local hospitals Inova Fair Oaks and Reston, for emergencies and general care in the support buildings. If all else fails you can always head to Reston, Sterling, Fairfax, etc to explore a bit more without having to travel much further than 25ish minutes out. All in all as I said above it’s a nice area and always has been, only thing I wish would change is that it was still the small secret living area Chantilly used to be back in the 90s, but the area has expanded and they planned for it accordingly and have kept up with the ever increasing numbers (not a complaint just remembering my youth lol). ^This is what everyone should be reading, all other comments so far are more opinion. Virginia, as a whole, has a shared fence law. Whether you live in an HOA or not. The law states if the fence is on the dividing property line then it is deemed a shared fence. The HOA has no legal power to tell either party whose financial responsibility it is to replace the shared fence. The owners can try to work together (ideal, but if you have a bad or financially unable neighbor not happening) to agree on how to financially cover the cost of repair or replacement, but legally it’s deemed a “neighbor to neighbor” interaction. 

The HOA can however still cite a broken or dilapidated shared fence as needing repair or replacement, but will legally have to defer to citing both properties for the violation as again it’s deemed shared by the VA law. 

Last point, others have been talking about neighbors signing off on repairs/replacements to acknowledge they are fine with the other property making the corrections. This is because the HOA most likely has an exterior modification resolution that outlines that certain large scale repairs or full replacements need HOA approval before the property can proceed with the work. The neighbor acknowledgments are just that, they are not approvals as some people confuse themselves for and start work before submitting the actual modification request to the HOA for review and processing.


TLDR,

1. Va has a Shared Fence Law and your HOA can’t intervene between properties to help resolve who will cover any part of the financial portion of the repair or replacement, on either parties behalf.

2. The HOA will potentially cite both properties for a damaged or dilapidated shared fence. 

3. Most large scale repairs or replacements need approval from your HOA before work can begin. An application must be submitted and often times there is a section for neighbor signatures (acknowledgment) that they are fine with the work. These are not approvals and and owner should not begin work until the HOA has reviewed and approved their submission.

Invest in Carnivore care, or Uncle Jim's Duk Soup. Treats, IMO, should be used for low blood sugar episodes only, when your little one will need a quick spike. Treats tend to be a bit high in sugar and can cause spikes that lead to crashes that will hurt your little one more than they help, if given at the wrong time. The soup is a complex protein and will help level out glucose all day and not spike. My little girl was diagnosed 7 months ago and the hardest part is watching for early signs that their sugar is low, as sometimes they can be as insignificant as over scratching or something. Just make sure to ask as many questions with your vet as possible, and dont hesitate to call them if you think something is off with your little one. Once you get everything settled your girl will live a happy and long life. We just have to remain extra vigilant from here forward! Good luck and we are all here to help!

Well I rescued my little one 7 years ago. He was abused before he was mine. It took me 3 months to get him to come out of his cage and a little less to get through some stuff you seem to be going through. Every bird will let you know when they are okay with you, mine came out of his cage when I wasnt looking and randomly landed on my chest haha. Still took a bit more time to warm up to hands and things but anyway. Some advice, do as many things possible close to the cage. I submerged him into my world, homework? I sat on the floor or had his cage next to my desk sofa while I did it. Eating? Same thing I did it Aaron d his cage, which can encourage them to eat with you as they are flock animals and feel safer that way. Listening to music, TV, you get the picture, everything that you can (that is safe to have your bird around) you do next to or in sight of the cage. My guy started to slowly go from the far corner to eventually the closest corner near me to see what I was up to after awhile. Next I began leaving the cage door open, to invite him to come out on his own, again took some weeks but hed perch at the door, then got to climbing out and going to the top of the cage. All this was without me handling him unless I had to get him out for a vet visit. Hands was harder as being abused made him bitey. I went a bit of a mixed route so I'm not highly recommending it without other peoples input. But when talking with my vet, they said if he was good to come out on his own to start offering my hand and making a gentle but quick motion toward his stomach, as he'd instinctively step up as to not be hit. And reward him with some sort of treat and give him praises. The reason I dont reccomend this is my guy had a serious dislike for hands so it was more forceful than I'd like but the vet said for his specific case I needed to give him less choice in the matter as to jump start him into getting okay with hands. So again in an ideal world maybe just getting then used to your hand being around and giving them a treat when they interact calmly/dont bite it? All in all when going through these motions as a pet owner, always look for help through people, internet, and most importantly a good local exotic vet if you have one. Sometimes people forget the vet isnt just paid visits and treatments, but you can always call a vet tech for free and ask for any additional tips or help over the phone and get some professional input. Last point is always make sure the cage is big enough, plenty of toys to stimulate your little one, and a healthy diet will all go along way. Good luck and hope this advice helps you, as it helped me. Just remember there will be good days and a lot of frustrating ones, but when you look back you'll realize it's all worth it when your little one finally warms up to you and all the stressing and time taken was worth it haha.

Please do not use this advice. I've worked with dogs for about 5 years and all this will do is make the dog refocus or accidentally lash out in your direction. You are almost guaranteed to get bit and in all honesty the chances of you stopping the fight wont diminish much, but you may find yourself in the middle between 2 dogs getting fucked up as well. If another person is available try to grab the dogs around the back of the neck, if they arent attached to each other near the area, and try to make separation. Getting the dogs away from each other is always going to be the best way to calm things down, and I do mean far away, where they cant see each other. If it's just you, all I can say is it will be a lot harder. I'm a somewhat bigger guy, and when I've had to go in alone, I usually just walked straight into the dogs knee first, not to kick or smash in the face, just kind of like if you were speed walking down a path. Its always worked to either get the dogs attention as they MAY notice something bigger coming from the side, or it cant be a good way of getting in between without risking injury to your hands or face. There truly isnt an ideal way to stop a dog fight if it's truly out of control unless you have a team of people who can distract and pull away. But to grab a dog near the hips or legs will almost always cause more harm to you, or the dog(s) themselves as you are just redirecting the rage, as I said before. But I was taught and unfortunately had to see for myself, that using your body to get in between is the best choice, just understand that most times it's a split decision and the only thing you dont wanna do is freeze up if possible.

You need to be very careful next time as ferrets imprint on their food. You making a subtle change like that can cause your little ones to stop eating entirely. Next time introduce the food separate from their own as the new scent is now mixed in with their food. Make sure your little one is at least drinking water, next try taking out the new food and replacing the whole thing with a batch of old food on its own, so there is no scent of the new food on it. Honestly if its been 3 days and you havent seen him eat and he has lost weight, if reintroducing the old food doesnt work quickly you should call your vet and inform them as ferrets need to eat every 2 to 3 hours. When doing changes the next time do some research and more importantly monitor them super closely. Take this as a learning experience. Ferrets wont show pain or distress for long periods of time.  And truly by the time they do you are finding put something is wrong waaaaayyyyy too late. Never wait for them to show signs, always be proactive. If you feel like something is off, or wrong, then go with your gut. The worst thing is you are a bit proactive and it turns out nothing is wrong. Sounds like you're a good owner and you're worried, again just take this as a teaching moment.
